subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Vocabulary development and comprehension: new students’ worries
outcomes: Match new words from the text with their meanings
Use the new words in your own sentences
Answer questions about new students' worries and solutions

tf.why: Apprehensive means worried about something, not excited.

tf.s: 'Homesickness' is sadness because you miss your home and family.
A 'deadline' is the time by which work must be finished.
tf.why: Right, after the deadline it is too late.

tf.s: To 'prioritise' means to do the easiest jobs first.
tf.why: Prioritise means you deal with the most important things first.

tf.s: The text says new students often feel excited but terrified.
tf.why: Yes, they have mixed feelings about starting university.

tf.s: 'Independence' means relying on other people for everything.
tf.why: Independence means looking after yourself without help.

tf.s: Getting lost is one problem new students may face.
tf.why: Yes, a new campus can be confusing.

tf.s: The text says new students cannot get help from anyone.
tf.why: They can ask other students, tutors or support services.

tf.s: Joining clubs and societies is the text's advice for making friends.
tf.why: Correct, clubs help you meet people.

tf.s: Student support services can help new students with problems.
tf.why: Yes, that is what support services are for.

boxes.q: Complete: 'She missed the ___ for her essay.'
boxes.why: A deadline is the last day to hand in work.

boxes.q: Complete: 'He felt ___ before his first exam.'
boxes.why: Apprehensive means worried, which fits before an exam.

boxes.q: Complete: 'The library is in the middle of the university ___.'
boxes.why: The campus is the university's land and buildings.
Living alone teaches you to manage on your own.

boxes.q: You have many tasks this week. What should you do with them?
boxes.why: Doing the most important tasks first helps you cope.

boxes.q: Complete: 'After a month away, he felt strong ___ and called his family.'
Which worry of new students is mentioned in the text?
boxes.why: Forgetting a deadline is a real worry for new students.
Anxiety is a strong feeling of worry.

boxes.q: Complete: 'Fear, joy and anger are all ___.'
boxes.why: These are all feelings, or emotions.

boxes.q: Who can a new student ask for help?
boxes.why: Tutors are there to help students.

o: The grounds and buildings of a university
mcq.why: The campus is where the university buildings are.

mcq.q: Which of these is a problem new students may face?
mcq.why: With so many new tasks, deadlines are easy to forget.

mcq.q: Which word from the text means 'feelings'?
mcq.why: Emotions are feelings like fear or happiness.

mcq.q: According to the text, who can new students ask for help?
o: Other students, tutors or support services
mcq.why: Many people at university are ready to help.

mcq.q: Sara has an essay, a test and a club meeting. She does the essay first because it is due tomorrow. What is she doing?
mcq.why: She is dealing with the most important task first.

mcq.q: Ali misses his family and feels sad in his new room. What is he feeling?
Mona forgot to hand in her project on time. What did she miss?
mcq.why: The deadline is the time the work must be handed in.

mcq.q: Why might joining clubs and societies help a new student?
o: They meet people and make friends
mcq.why: Clubs bring together people with the same interests.

mcq.q: Why could a new student feel 'excited but terrified'?
o: University is a new experience with many changes
mcq.why: New experiences bring both excitement and worry.

mcq.q: Why is it important to prioritise at university?
o: Students have many tasks and deadlines
mcq.why: With many tasks, you must decide what comes first.
